title: Domain, Range, and Graph of the Greatest Integer Floor of Sine
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph y = \sin x and the greatest integer function y = \lfloor \sin x \rfloor together. Determine the domain and range of \lfloor \sin x \rfloor.

steps.title: Determine the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Both y = sin x and the floor function are defined for all real numbers, so the composite function y = floor(sin x) has domain (-infinity, infinity).
steps.why: Every real number x produces a real output sin x, which has a unique greatest integer <= sin x.

steps.title: Analyze Possible Output Values of sin x
steps.explanation: As x ranges over R, sin x takes values strictly within the closed interval [-1, 1].
steps.why: The unit circle bounds the vertical coordinate sin x between -1 and 1.

steps.title: Evaluate the Floor Function Across [-1, 1] to Find the Range
steps.explanation: When sin x is in [-1, 0), floor(sin x) = -1; when sin x is in [0, 1), floor(sin x) = 0; and at the isolated peaks x = pi/2 + 2k*pi where sin x = 1, floor(sin x) = 1. Thus the range is the three-element set {-1, 0, 1}.
steps.why: By definition, floor(u) is the greatest integer less than or equal to u.
